chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a person with a sense of honour, and I (peace be upon him) am with a more sense of honour than him, and Allah (exalted be He) would stub the nose of the one who does not have a sense of honour, from the Believers and the Muslims'.

key_terms.أَغْيَرُ: More having a sense of honour / more zealous
key_terms.جَدَعَ اللَّهُ أَنْفَ: Allah stubs the nose of (a phrase indicating humiliation)
key_terms.غَيُوراً: Having a sense of honour or zeal for what is right

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Ghayrah (sense of honour) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of 'ghayrah' (zealous honor), claiming superiority over Prophet Ibrahim to highlight the comprehensive nature of his prophetic mission. The warning of Allah 'stubbing the nose' of those lacking this trait underscores 'ghayrah' as a fundamental spiritual and social virtue in Shia tradition, essential for maintaining communal integrity and personal piety. This concept is not merely emotional jealousy but a protective zeal for the dignity of the believer and the boundaries set by God.
